titre: Magna Carta (1215): Declared Void by the Pope Ten Weeks Later
accroche: Sealed on June 15, 1215, the charter is declared void on August 24 by Innocent III. It does not receive the name Magna Carta until 1217.
contenu_vulgarise:
On June 15, 1215, in the meadow of Runnymede, between Windsor and Staines, King John of England grants a charter to his barons. The document is not signed: it is authenticated by the great seal, affixed by officers rather than by the king himself. Seventy days later, a letter from the pope declares it void.

## A Charter of Feudal Grievances

The 1215 charter has sixty-three clauses, according to the numbering that Blackstone gave his critical edition of 1759. It looks less like a declaration of principles than a list of scores to settle between the king and his barons. Clause 12 forbids levying scutage or aid without the common counsel of the realm. Clause 1 guarantees the freedom of the English Church, and recalls that the king had obtained ratification of this from Pope Innocent III before the quarrel with his barons. Clause 39 is the most quoted: no free man shall be taken, imprisoned, dispossessed, exiled or destroyed in any way, except by the lawful judgment of his peers or by the law of the land. According to Wikipedia, its style and content draw on the Charter of Liberties of Henry I and other charters of the period. Clause 61 creates a council of twenty-five barons charged with overseeing the king's compliance with his commitments.

## From Sealing to War

John quickly turns to Rome: in July, he asks for the pope's help, arguing that the charter infringes the pope's rights as the king's feudal overlord. Less than three months after the agreement, John and the barons who had remained loyal to him repudiate it, and the First Barons' War breaks out. According to Wikipedia, a letter from Innocent III dated August 24, which reached England at the end of September, judges the charter shameful, illegal and unjust since the king had been forced into it, and declares it null and devoid of all validity forever. In it the pope threatens with excommunication any king who observed it and any barons who sought to have it enforced. The king dies on the night of October 18, 1216, leaving a nine-year-old heir, Henry III.

## The Text That Survives

It is then that the document's life begins. In 1216, Henry III's regency reissues it, stripped of some of its most radical content. In 1217, the charter is part of the Treaty of Lambeth peace agreement, where it takes the name “Magna Carta.” In 1225, short of money, Henry reissues it again, in exchange for a new tax.

The name Magna Carta thus dates not from Runnymede but from 1217, and the numbering into sixty-three clauses from 1759.

repere.texte: Between the sealing of Magna Carta on June 15, 1215, and the letter from Innocent III declaring it void, dated August 24, 70 days pass, exactly ten weeks.

quiz.question: What becomes of the 1215 charter after it is sealed at Runnymede?
choix: It remains in force without interruption until King John's death in 1216
Innocent III confirms it and places it under the protection of the English Church
Innocent III declares it void, then it is reissued in 1216, 1217 and 1225
It remains a dead letter, having never received any royal seal
quiz.explication: The great seal is affixed on June 15, 1215, but a letter from Innocent III dated August 24 declares the charter void, and war breaks out. It is then reissued in 1216, 1217 and 1225: so it was neither applied without interruption, nor confirmed by the pope, nor left without a seal.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Why does King John appeal to the pope in July 1215, shortly after sealing the charter?
choix: He asks the pope to confirm the charter in order to calm his barons
He argues that the charter infringes the pope's rights as the king's feudal overlord
He wants the pope to excommunicate the rebel barons on the spot
He seeks to have his son Henry recognized as his legitimate heir
quiz_supplementaire.explication: John argues that the charter infringes the rights of the pope, overlord of the king of England since the ratification obtained earlier. The text does not say that he seeks a confirmation, an immediate excommunication, or recognition of his son.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does clause 39 of the 1215 Magna Carta, the most quoted in the text, guarantee?
choix: That every man, free or not, has the right to a fair trial before the king himself
That no free man will be imprisoned except by the judgment of his peers or the law of the land
That the barons may henceforth levy tax or aid without the king's consent
That the English Church is exempt forever from any tax levied by the king
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Clause 39 guarantees that no free man will be taken, imprisoned or dispossessed except by the lawful judgment of his peers or the law of the land. The right to a trial before the king, the barons' taxation and the Church's tax exemption belong to other clauses or do not appear in the text.
